subject: ventures/shopify-a11y-evidence
professional: an IAAP-certified accessibility auditor (CPACC/WAS) who writes WCAG 2.2 AA conformance and remediation reports for e-commerce storefronts; first checks: does the evidence record carry the scan's own timestamp, engine version, ruleset scope and the failing elements; are WCAG failures separated from axe best-practice rules; does a before/after diff compare like with like; are legal claims (ADA, EAA, overlays) stated without overclaim

evidence.correctness: Ran the shipped modules on hand-built axe-core exports whose rule ids, impacts and tags were copied from the axe-core 4.10.0 package's own rule metadata (npm tarball, axe.js lines 31098-31681) (`node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/28cabc82-884b-5f5d-b359-081413dc958d/scratchpad/shopify-a11y-evidence/scripts/run.mjs`). Arithmetic recomputes exactly: counts 4 rules / 7 nodes, impact 2 critical 1 serious 1 moderate; quote sample 3.25 h raw, 3.9 h buffered, $497.25/$585/$731.25; a second quote at $120, 10%, 1.4x hand-recomputes to 7.49 h, 8.24 h, $840.48/$988.80/$1,236.00 with weights 9/8/4/2. Wrong where it matters to an auditor: the record's 'Checked:' date is the day the record is generated, not the export's `timestamp` (axe.d.ts:465 AxeResults.timestamp), so a 2026-03-01 scan is recorded as checked 2026-11-17; the compare diff counts a rule that moved from violations to incomplete, on a different URL, as 'Resolved'; theme routing sends Dawn's header account icon to 'Account / login' (main-login.liquid) and Dawn's cart-drawer checkout button to 'Checkout ... not a theme Liquid file', and never matches the bare selectors '#search' and '#cart' (the `\b#` patterns cannot match after a space or at string start).
evidence.completeness: All four pages the README lists exist and work end to end through their modules: evidence record (buildReport/reportAsText, copy, download, incomplete section), quote (quoteRemediation/quoteAsText, rate, buffer, theme multiplier), theme areas (groupByThemeArea), before/after compare (compareReports/comparisonAsText), plus vs-accessibe.html and the opt-out usage counters with a remembered preference. No TODOs, stubs or dead internal links found; the ../ada-title-ii-evidence/ sibling link resolves to ventures/ada-title-ii-evidence. served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder or retired origin in the deployed llms.txt/sitemap/robots/canonicals (the github.io links in source llms.txt are rewritten at deploy: source-only, not filed).
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 68 tests, 68 pass, 0.29 s. Seven seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: compare nodeDelta sign flip CAUGHT, quote high multiplier 1.25->1.2 CAUGHT, extra-node hours off-by-one CAUGHT, incomplete count from violations CAUGHT; theme-area score ignoring impact weight (score += 1) SURVIVED, dropping the /\bfooter\b/ pattern SURVIVED, removing the WCAG tag label from every record line SURVIVED. 3 of 7 survived: the theme-area ranking that picks 'Open first' and the WCAG mapping in the evidence record are unpinned.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (191 lines), quote.mjs (149), theme-areas.mjs (211), usage.mjs, index.html, quote.html, theme-areas.html, what-changed-between-axe-scans.html, vs-accessibe.html and the test files. Small pure modules, no dependencies, storage guarded. Defects: browserStorage() and the usage recorder are copied verbatim between quote.mjs and theme-areas.mjs, and IMPACT_WEIGHT is duplicated; theme-areas.mjs:122 keeps an unrecognised impact string ('High') while calc.mjs maps it to 'unknown', so the two pages disagree on the same export; buildReport accepts any object ({foo:1} or []) and returns a clean 'No violations were present' record instead of rejecting a paste that is not an axe export; 'Needs review: 1 rules' plural.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'nothing leaves this browser' (backed: no fetch in modules, page tests); 'not a compliance determination' (backed: every text output ends with it, calc.mjs:92, quote.mjs:130, theme-areas.mjs:192, calc.mjs:188); ADA/WCAG FAQ answers 'No' to compliance proof and names axe's blind spots (backed, careful); no EAA claim made; ADA Title II sibling link correctly ties Title II to WCAG 2.1 AA (28 CFR 35.200); no-warranty and no-SLA footers on every page; vs-accessibe.html states non-affiliation and makes no effectiveness or legal claim. Not backed: the core claim of a 'dated ... evidence record' (README:3, index.html:6) dates the record, not the test; theme-areas.html:71 headline 'Open the Liquid file the scan is actually pointing at' overstates a selector heuristic that misroutes Dawn's own header and cart-drawer markup (the body text does qualify it); compare page sample tags 'label' as serious/wcag332 and link-in-text-block as moderate, where axe-core 4.10 ships critical/wcag412 and serious.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job as an agency auditor handing a merchant a record: paste an export, get rule ids, impact, node counts, raw wcag tags and helpUrls, copy or download. Usable as a summary, not as evidence: the record has no scan timestamp, no ruleset scope (toolOptions.runOnly, e.g. wcag2a/wcag2aa), no testEnvironment (viewport, user agent), and no failing element targets or HTML, so a developer receiving it cannot find the elements and a reviewer cannot tell what was tested when. The quote page is a usable planning aid with disclosed, uncited hour constants. The compare page gives a quick rule-level diff but would let a merchant claim 'resolved' for a rule that moved to needs-review or a scan of a different page.
evidence.domain: Compared against WCAG-EM (W3C evaluation methodology: record scope, date, tools and versions, sample of pages) and axe-core's result model. Departures: axe 'best-practice' rules (e.g. landmark-one-main) are counted under 'Violations' with no label, where an auditor separates WCAG failures from advisories; wcag tags are printed raw ('wcag143') instead of mapped to SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), Level AA; the diff is keyed on rule id only, so two fixed nodes replaced by two new ones reads 'same node count'; violation->incomplete moves are 'resolved'. The vs-accessibe page says a merchant 'can reasonably want both' an overlay and an audit without mentioning the practitioner consensus against overlays (Overlay Fact Sheet) or the FTC's 2025 order against accessiBe over WCAG-compliance claims, which an accessibility professional would cite. Automated-only coverage is disclosed throughout, which is correct practice.

defects.what: The evidence record's 'Checked:' date is the day the record is generated, not the axe export's timestamp: a March scan pasted in November is recorded as checked in November. The product's core claim is a dated record of the test.

Before/after diff treats a rule absent from the later violations as 'Resolved' even when it moved to incomplete (needs review) or the later scan is of a different URL; no URL-mismatch warning; rule-id keying hides node-level change ('same node count' when different elements fail).

Theme-area routing misroutes Dawn's own markup: header account icon (href /account/login) goes to Account/login, cart-drawer checkout button (name=checkout) goes to Checkout 'not a theme Liquid file'; checkout and account patterns match html anywhere before header/cart.
Patterns /\b#cart\b/ and /\b#search\b/ can never match a bare '#cart' or '#search' selector (no word boundary before '#' after a space or at start); those nodes fall to Unclassified.
Evidence record omits what an auditor needs to use it as evidence: failing element targets/HTML, ruleset scope (toolOptions.runOnly), testEnvironment, and the scan timestamp.
axe best-practice rules (e.g. landmark-one-main) are counted as Violations with no label; the record does not separate WCAG failures from advisories or map wcag tags to success criteria and level.
Any JSON object (or array) that is not an axe export produces a clean 'No violations were present' record instead of an error, so a wrong paste yields a clean-looking evidence record.
Theme-area ranking (impact-weighted score that picks 'Open first'), the footer pattern and the WCAG tag label in the record are untested: three seeded mutants survived.
Headline 'Open the Liquid file the scan is actually pointing at' overstates a selector heuristic (body text qualifies it).
Compare-page sample export tags 'label' as serious/wcag332 and link-in-text-block as moderate; axe-core 4.10.0 ships label critical/wcag412 and link-in-text-block serious.
theme-areas keeps an unrecognised impact string verbatim while calc.mjs maps it to 'unknown'; usage recorder and browserStorage copied between quote.mjs and theme-areas.mjs.
Remediation hour constants per impact are uncited (disclosed as a planning estimate).

vs-accessibe page says a merchant 'can reasonably want both' an overlay and an audit without noting the practitioner consensus against overlays or the FTC's 2025 order against accessiBe over WCAG-compliance claims.

verdict: A small, clean, honestly disclaimed set of four browser-local pages that summarise an axe-core export. The arithmetic recomputes exactly (counts, impact split, two quote scenarios hand-checked) and its legal language is careful: it never claims ADA, WCAG or EAA compliance. It does not reach an IAAP auditor's bar for an evidence record: the record dates itself rather than the scan (axe timestamp ignored), omits element targets, ruleset scope and environment, and mixes best-practice rules into violations; the diff calls a rule 'resolved' when it moved to needs-review or the later scan is of another page; theme routing misroutes Dawn's own header and cart-drawer markup. 68 tests pass but 3 of 7 seeded mutants survived. Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2, median 2); finished (completeness 3).
